corpus_authoring_fixes_disclosed: 16 mismatches were found and fixed during pre-freeze verification, all before this hash was taken: (1) several responsibility-lead test sentences lacked any competency vocabulary or any _QUALIFYING_INTENT_V2 cue word at all, so they declined as no_competency_language before ever reaching the responsibility_lead check they were meant to exercise -- reworded to include both a real competency phrase and a 'strong' cue word while still opening with a bare imperative verb. (2) Several LEARNING-section / unsectioned-preamble / unsectioned-document test sentences used 'strong exposure to X'/'deep expertise in X' phrasing that never became a Claim at all outside a recognized REQUIRED/PREFERRED/RESPONSIBILITY section, because segmentation.py's own _looks_like_requirement vocabulary does not include 'strong'/'exposure'/'understanding' even though competency_extraction.py's own _QUALIFYING_INTENT_V2 gate does -- reworded to 'Familiarity with X'/'Experience with X' (which pass both gates) EXCEPT for one control (p19's 'Strong understanding of concurrency.') which was deliberately KEPT with a corrected expect_no_claim=true expectation, specifically to record this genuine integration-interface mismatch as a disclosed Phase 6 finding rather than hide it. (3) One narrative-rejection test sentence ('Lead the team with...') accidentally collided with the pre-existing _BROADER_NARRATIVE_SUBJECT pattern's literal 'the team' branch -- reworded to 'the group'. (4) One applicability-condition control's expected projection was corrected from job_requirement to unparsed_claim: project_qualification's own pre-existing, unmodified safety rule routes ANY applicability condition to UnparsedClaim, which the original expectation had wrongly assumed otherwise. (5) One control's expected tag set was corrected to include BOTH system-design and distributed-systems: 'distributed architecture' is simultaneously system-design's own canonical phrase and a pre-existing distributed-systems alias, a genuine, disclosed cross-tag vocabulary overlap discovered during verification, not introduced by this milestone. None of these are code changes -- all are corpus-authoring corrections, made and verified before this freeze. After the first freeze (hash b30a7c0e...) a coverage gap was found: Phase 2's own required category list (named technologies, education) had no dedicated controls. Posting p28 (4 controls) was added to close this gap, re-verified with zero mismatches, and the corpus was re-frozen under the sha256 above -- the only post-first-freeze addition.
